_comment: Shared callsign validation vectors, asserted from both languages.
The browser transmit gate (isValidCallsign in src/dsp/bandPlan.ts) decides whether a
station may key up. Three other implementations - both React settings modals and the
Python setup wizard - used to carry a LOOSER pattern, so the wizard showed a green
'Valid ITU Callsign' for callsigns the gate refuses at slot start, and a red 'Invalid'
for ones it permits. An operator who trusts the wizard and then cannot transmit has been
told two different things by one program.
The three disagreements the audit measured are the first three 'divergence' cases below.
extra_rule: The base prefix (the part before any trailing '/suffix') must contain a letter.
_limits: This is a STRUCTURAL check, not an allocation lookup: it rejects an empty box, a name
typed into the callsign field and obvious typos, which is what the transmit gate needs.
It cannot tell whether a well-formed callsign was actually issued to the operator, and
well-formed strings that are not real callsigns (e.g. '111A') pass. Do not add cases here
